answer: To resist Sybil swarms, the network anchors identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating identity across a porous, karst-like graph of agent interactions ensures trust. Minting identity clones incurs exponential capital exhaustion, making attacks cost-prohibitive. Valid identities anchor like structural timber, running under velvet-smooth verification while superlinear staking costs bankrupt attackers.
